newsitem.title: USA: US corp debt mart eerily quiet, FOMC jitters begin.
newsitem.headline: US corp debt mart eerily quiet, FOMC jitters begin.

text.p: Corporate bond primary sector activity is expected to remain eerily calm as the Federal Reserve policy-makers get set to vote on U.S. monetary policy, players said.
The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the Fed's policy-setting arm, will vote on whether to tighten interest rates to guard against inflation or leave monetary policy unchanged.
A rate increase would mean higher borrowing costs for U.S. corporations looking to finance debt in the corporate bond primary market.
"If it goes well and the Fed doesn't do anything, then it's going to become more of an issuers' market and we'll see issuance pick up after the holiday," one high-grade syndicate source said.
"However, if they don't tighten, the market will take it to mean that there's going to be one later on, so it'll depend on what they say following the meeting," he added.
A Reuter poll shows that U.S. experts are about equally divided over whether the Fed will maintain policy as it stands or hike rates by 25 basis points.
